notes: The iOS 26.5 runtime is installed (proof 0 reads `xcrun simctl list runtimes`). The phone checks run on the simulator through scripts/iphone-rig.sh (docs/lanes/iphone-rig.md): it uses only `xcrun simctl` (no Simulator.app, no `open`), creates its own device 'Whoosh rig iPhone 17 Pro', launches the app with --fixture-core and a private socket folder, exports WHOOSH_SOCKET_DIR and WHOOSH_IPHONE_SOCKET_DIR, runs the command, then terminates the app and shuts the device down. Proof 1 is the script's own selftest with a fake xcrun (launches nothing). Proofs 2 to 6 are the lead's run on the real simulator, one per phone check, each printing its totals line. Each parity check is also run once on a broken copy to be seen red: a throwaway worktree with `refreshedAt = Date()` at Sources/Features/InboxPhone/InboxPhoneState.swift:79 changed to `refreshedAt = refreshedAt`, built into another <out>, run with proof 3's command; it must print `1 failed` for par-inboxphone-refresh/refresh-reads-again (declared at checks/parity/par-inboxphone.py:78). Search check: `--live` is the flag at checks/searchphone-check.py:1298 (without it the check runs on its stand-in); the lead confirms by the run's own output. Shots at 402x874 (docs/design/geometry/iphone-inbox.json:4-7): see docs/lanes/iphone-rig.md, they are read as pictures by the lead. | Round 2: the rig now uninstalls the app after the boot and before the install (a fresh container every run), the default app arguments are the lead's (--fixture-core -AppleLanguages (en) -AppleLocale en_US); proofs 7 to 9 are the pictures tool's selftest, the one-command round's selftest and the round itself.
